## Purpose and status

This is an internal `fplida` explainer for the ATO Personal Income Tax (PIT)
datasets. PIT is not a single file in PLIDA. In the current package it covers
three related products:

- `PIT_PS`, Payment Summaries;
- `PIT_ITR`, Income Tax Returns;
- `PIT_IE`, ABS Derived Income.

The note records what these synthetic products are intended to represent, how
the main variables should be interpreted, and which source documents justify
those interpretations. It is deliberately stored under `inst/internal-docs/`
rather than `vignettes/` so it is available inside the package source and
installed package, but is not yet promoted as a user-facing vignette.

The current PIT implementation is compact and analysis-oriented. It does not
emit every historical PIT variable in the PLIDA Data Item List (DIL). This is
different from the current STP implementation, which is closer to raw DIL-style
products. This note therefore documents both:

- the current `fplida` output columns; and
- the official PLIDA/ATO concepts those columns are meant to approximate.

If the PIT generators are later made fully DIL-shaped, this note should be
updated so the variable tables use the raw DIL names as the primary names and
the compact names only as historical notes.

| Product area | What the research source supports | What is still not found |
|---|---|---|
| PIT_PS payment summaries | ATO payment-summary and withholding sources support payment-summary concepts such as gross payments, tax withheld, reportable fringe benefits, reportable employer superannuation contributions, and lump sums. Local DIL metadata provides same-dataset crosswalks for ten compact generated PIT_PS fields. | I did not find same-dataset PIT_PS metadata support for generated `UNION_FEES` or `WORKPLACE_GIVING`; they remain external-source concepts, not source-equivalent PIT_PS variables. |
| PIT_ITR tax returns | ATO myTax and tax-return sources support the broad income, deduction, offset, Medicare levy, and taxable-income concepts in the compact ITR generator. | The guide still needs exact local DIL-to-tax-return item citations for every simplified tax calculation component before it can be treated as a complete ATO tax calculator. |
| PIT_IE derived income | ABS administrative-income sources support the role of PS and ITR in derived administrative income estimates. | I did not find a public source that validates the current generated edited-income noise model or all component distributions. |
| Superannuation fields | ATO sources distinguish reportable employer superannuation contributions from ordinary compulsory super guarantee amounts. | Generated `SUPER_GUARANTEE` remains local SG-style logic and is not source-equivalent to `PIT_PS/RPRTBL_EMPLYR_SUPER_CNTRBN_AMT`. |

## Product structure

### PIT products in PLIDA and fplida

| Dataset | Official role | Current fplida role |
|---|---|---|
| `PIT_PS` | Payment-summary records submitted to the ATO by employers or other payers. A person can have more than one row in a financial year. | Annual person-employer payment-summary records used to model employer-linked wage income and PAYG withholding. |
| `PIT_ITR` | Annual individual income tax returns lodged by taxpayers, including income, deductions, offsets, tax liabilities, tax withheld, and debts. | Annual person-level lodged-return records built from `PIT_PS` aggregates, filing probabilities, and synthetic tax-return components. |
| `PIT_IE` | ABS derived income, built from ITR and PS data to align with ABS income definitions. | Annual person-level derived income components and earner flags. |

ABS describes ITR as annual information submitted by taxpayers, with incomplete
coverage where people have not lodged or are not required to lodge. ABS
describes PS as financial-year income, tax withheld, and related information for
people who received an income statement or PAYG payment summary from an
employer and whose summary was submitted to the ATO. ABS also notes that ATO
supplies ITR and PS data in 12-month and later 16-month extracts, where the
later extract is more complete.

### Output folders and file format

The current generators write parquet only. The output folders are:

| Dataset | Output folder | Main generator |
|---|---|---|
| `PIT_PS` | `ato-pit_ps/` | `generate_pit_ps()` |
| `PIT_ITR` | `ato-pit_itr/` | `generate_pit_itr()` |
| `PIT_IE` | `ato-pit_ie/` | `generate_pit_ie()` |

Each folder also receives an ATO agency spine file from `write_agency_spine()`.
The PIT generators use the ATO person identifier from the synthetic spine.

### Financial-year coverage

The local metadata and current generator defaults differ because the metadata
represents the DIL inventory while the generator default is a modelling choice.

| Dataset | Local DIL coverage | Current generator default |
|---|---:|---:|
| `PIT_PS` | 2001-02 to 2022-23 in `datasets.csv`; product names also include later current-DIL naming variants. | FY end years `2010:2024`. |
| `PIT_ITR` | 1999-2000 to 2023-24. | FY end years `2010:2024`. |
| `PIT_IE` | 2010-11 to 2023-24. | FY end years `2011:2023`. |

For a financial-year end year `2015`, the reference period is FY 2014-15.
The package uses a mixture of integer year fields and financial-year strings,
so downstream code should normalise year labels explicitly before joining
tables.

### ITR sub-tables

Official PLIDA PIT_ITR is split into several year-specific tables. The core
current `fplida` ITR output writes four sub-tables per year:

| Table type | Concept | Current fplida columns |
|---|---|---|
| `context` | Person-year tax-return context. | Person ID, income year, occupation, industry, resident indicator. |
| `inc-loss` | Income and loss items. | Salary/wages, business income, interest income, taxable income or loss. |
| `ded-exp-off` | Deductions, expenses, and offsets input items. | Work deductions, work-deduction components, gifts, other deductions. |
| `whld-debt` | Tax withheld and debts/tax outcomes. | Gross tax, low-income offset, Medicare levy, net tax, balance payable/refundable. |

The 19 March 2026 DIL contains many more ITR variables than the compact
generator emits. It also contains historical table variants, 12-month and
16-month extracts, wages-and-salaries tables, and geography helper tables. Do
not infer that an omitted official DIL item is zero in real PLIDA data; it is
only absent from the current synthetic generator.

## Variable-level schema register

Every generated variable observed in this pass for this guide is listed in
[`schema-registers/schema-register-pit.csv`](schema-registers/schema-register-pit.csv).
The register records R type, sampled generated missingness, sampled generated
domains/distributions, and direct PLIDA metadata matches. Treat those sampled
domains/distributions as implementation evidence only, not as official ATO/ABS
income data.

A rendered variable evidence appendix for this guide is available at [`variable-evidence-appendices/pit-variable-evidence.qmd`](variable-evidence-appendices/pit-variable-evidence.qmd). It contains one row per generated variable with observed generated values or distributions, local metadata/crosswalk status, and unresolved-source caveats.

| Dataset | Generated variable rows | Direct PLIDA metadata matches | No direct PLIDA name match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `PIT_IE` | 16 | 16 | 0 |
| `PIT_ITR` | 28 | 27 | 1 |
| `PIT_PS` | 14 | 1 | 13 |

PIT coverage now comes from a targeted non-empty FY2021 run under
`/tmp/fplida-pit-schema/fplida_12k`: `PIT_PS` has 5,990 generated rows,
`PIT_ITR` has 5,223 filer rows in each of the four ITR sub-tables, and
`PIT_IE` has 6,055 rows. `PIT_PS` remains the weakest crosswalk surface:
most compact payment-summary fields do not directly match local PLIDA names
and should stay labelled as implementation fields until mapped to DIL names.

`generated-variable-crosswalk.csv` now records manual local metadata
crosswalks for ten compact `PIT_PS` fields: financial year, employer ABN,
gross payments, tax withheld, reportable FBT, allowances, and lump sums A/B/D/E.
It also maps `PIT_ITR` `INTST_AMT` to same-dataset `GRS_INTST_AMT`.
`SUPER_GUARANTEE` is deliberately labelled not source-equivalent: local PIT_PS
metadata contains `RPRTBL_EMPLYR_SUPER_CNTRBN_AMT`, but the generated field is
ordinary SG-style local logic rather than reportable employer superannuation
contributions. Public ATO concepts support union/professional-fee deductions
and workplace giving, and local STP metadata contains
`IDV_WRKPLC_GVING_TOTL_AMT`, but I did not find same-dataset `PIT_PS` metadata
support for generated `UNION_FEES` or `WORKPLACE_GIVING`. Treat both as
external-source concepts that are not source-equivalent PIT_PS variables.

## Core design principle

The generator should preserve the distinction between three different PIT data
concepts:

- `PIT_PS` observes payer-reported annual payment-summary information, usually
  at person-employer-year level.
- `PIT_ITR` observes lodged tax returns, so people who did not lodge are absent
  even when they have payment-summary income.
- `PIT_IE` is derived income constructed to align with ABS income concepts; it
  is not a raw ATO form extract.

Practical implications:

- Do not treat `PIT_PS` as a complete employment spell table. It is annual and
  payer-linked, but it does not always identify actual employment duration.
- Do not treat absence from `PIT_ITR` as zero income. It may mean the person did
  not lodge or was not required to lodge.
- Do not treat `PIT_IE` as a tax liability table. It is for income components
  and derived source flags, not tax assessment.
- Do not add together `PIT_PS` and `PIT_ITR` wage amounts without a clear
  reconciliation rule. ITR salary and wages often correspond to the aggregate
  of PS wage records, but they are distinct records with different reporting
  processes and amendment timing.

## Missingness, zeros, and top-coding

The current synthetic PIT generators mostly use zero for absent dollar
components within an observed row. Row absence carries the stronger meaning:

- no `PIT_PS` row means no generated payment summary for that person-payer-year;
- no `PIT_ITR` row means no generated lodged return for that person-year;
- no `PIT_IE` row means no generated derived-income row after the package's age
  and non-zero-income filters.

Missing values should therefore be interpreted cautiously. In current output,
missing often means a column is not part of the compact generator, not that the
real source concept is absent in PLIDA.

The current PIT generators do not apply explicit top-coding to income, tax, or
deduction variables. `TI_OR_LSS_AMT` is lower-bounded at `-50000` in the current
ITR generator; that is a synthetic floor on taxable loss, not an official
top-code. Unknown or unavailable occupation and industry context can be encoded
as zero strings such as `"000000"`, `"0000"`, or `"00"`.

For real PLIDA use, check the current DIL, DataLab user guide, and project
output rules for any confidentiality treatment, perturbation, suppression, or
top-coding that is not represented in this synthetic package.

## PIT_PS: Payment Summaries

### Row unit

`PIT_PS` is an annual payment-summary record. The current package creates one
row per person, employer, and financial year for generated employment records.
A person can have multiple rows in a year if they have multiple employers.

ABS uses PS data to estimate employee income from the relevant
`madipge-ato-d-pay-sum-fy...` table. In the ABS administrative-income method,
important PS items include period start and end dates, income type, gross
amount, reportable fringe benefits, reportable employer superannuation
contributions, lump-sum payments, allowances, exempt foreign employment income,
and employer identifiers. The current compact `fplida` output includes the
main annual amounts but does not include period dates or every DIL field.

### Current fplida variables

| Variable | Meaning and values | Missing, zeros, and subpopulation | Source concept |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SYNTHETIC_AEUID` | Synthetic ATO person identifier. | Present for every generated PS row. Join through the ATO agency spine for package-wide person identifiers. | PLIDA person identifier. |
| `FINANCIAL_YEAR` | Integer financial-year end year. `2015` means FY 2014-15. | Present for every generated row. Normalise before joining to `PIT_IE`, which uses a string year label. | PS income year or reference financial year. |
| `EMPLOYER_ABN` | Synthetic employer identifier. It is an employer or payer key, not a workplace/site key. | Present for every generated row. Multiple employers per person-year are possible. | DIL `ABN_HASH_TRUNC` or payer business number concept. |
| `GROSS_PAYMENTS` | Annual gross payments from the payer to the person. Numeric dollars. | Zero should mean no generated gross payment on an observed row, although current generated PS rows are normally positive. Missing would be a generation/schema issue. | DIL `GRS_AMT`; ATO payment-summary gross payments. |
| `TAX_WITHHELD` | PAYG tax withheld from the payment-summary income. Numeric dollars. | Zero can occur for low-income records or where withholding is not generated. It does not imply the payment was non-taxable. | DIL `TAX_WHELD_AMT`; ATO PAYG withholding. |
| `REPORTABLE_FBT` | Reportable fringe benefits amount. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated reportable fringe benefit. This is not assessable income, but ATO uses it in some income tests. | DIL `RPRTBL_FBT_AMT`; ATO RFBA. |
| `SUPER_GUARANTEE` | Current synthetic compulsory super guarantee style contribution, computed from gross pay using the package's SG rate table. | Zero means no generated SG amount. This differs from the official payment-summary `RPRTBL_EMPLYR_SUPER_CNTRBN_AMT`, which is reportable employer super and should not include ordinary compulsory SG. | Local generator concept; related but not identical to DIL reportable employer super. |
| `ALLOWANCES` | Total allowances. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated allowance. Whether allowances should be included in an earnings measure depends on the target income concept. | DIL `TOTL_ALWNC_AMT`; ATO payment-summary allowances. |
| `LUMP_SUM_A` | Lump sum A, generally unused leave and related payments on termination. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated lump sum A. | DIL `LSPA_AMT`; ATO NAT 0046. |
| `LUMP_SUM_B` | Lump sum B, unused long-service leave accrued before 16 August 1978. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated lump sum B. ATO instructions indicate only part of this amount is taxable. | DIL `LSPB_AMT`; ATO NAT 0046. |
| `LUMP_SUM_D` | Lump sum D, tax-free genuine redundancy or early retirement payment below the tax-free threshold. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated lump sum D. Do not include it as taxable wage income. | DIL `LSPD_AMT`; ATO NAT 0046. |
| `LUMP_SUM_E` | Lump sum E, back payment of certain amounts accrued more than 12 months earlier. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated lump sum E. | DIL `LSPE_AMT`; ATO NAT 0046. |
| `UNION_FEES` | Synthetic union or professional association fees. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated fee. This is closer to a deduction-support variable than a payment amount. | ATO union/professional-fee deduction concept; no same-dataset PIT_PS metadata found. |
| `WORKPLACE_GIVING` | Synthetic workplace-giving donation amount. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated workplace giving. Treat as a donation/deduction-related amount, not gross wages. | ATO workplace-giving concept and local STP `IDV_WRKPLC_GVING_TOTL_AMT`; no same-dataset PIT_PS metadata found. |

### Payment-summary components

The current compact variables are useful for annual payment-summary income and
employer-linked wage analysis. A conservative component construction is:

```r
ps_components <- pit_ps |>
  mutate(
    gross_payments = coalesce(GROSS_PAYMENTS, 0),
    allowances = coalesce(ALLOWANCES, 0),
    taxable_lump_sum_a = coalesce(LUMP_SUM_A, 0),
    taxable_lump_sum_b_component = 0.05 * coalesce(LUMP_SUM_B, 0),
    tax_free_lump_sum_d = coalesce(LUMP_SUM_D, 0),
    backpay_lump_sum_e = coalesce(LUMP_SUM_E, 0),
    tax_withheld = coalesce(TAX_WITHHELD, 0),
    reportable_fbt = coalesce(REPORTABLE_FBT, 0),
    synthetic_sg = coalesce(SUPER_GUARANTEE, 0),
    employee_cash_income =
      gross_payments + allowances +
      taxable_lump_sum_a + taxable_lump_sum_b_component + backpay_lump_sum_e
  )
```

This is not an official ABS current-income derivation. The ABS current-income
method uses PS period dates, checks employer validity against later STP data,
and applies divisor rules for partial-year records. The compact package output
does not currently contain enough PS date detail to reproduce that method
exactly.

## PIT_ITR: Income Tax Returns

### Row unit

`PIT_ITR` is an annual lodged-return dataset. The current generator first
aggregates `PIT_PS` gross payments and tax withheld by person-year, then applies
a filing-probability model. Low-income people are less likely to lodge,
especially when no tax was withheld. The generated ITR population is therefore
a subset of people with generated PS income, not the full synthetic population.

The current filing model uses the tax-free threshold as a key threshold. ATO
guidance describes the tax-free threshold as `$18,200` and indicates that tax
payable is worked out when a person lodges a return. The model is a synthetic
approximation only; real lodgement obligations depend on more circumstances
than annual wage income and tax withheld.

### Context table variables

| Variable | Meaning and values | Missing, zeros, and subpopulation | Source concept |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SYNTHETIC_AEUID` | Synthetic ATO person identifier. | Present for every generated ITR row. | PLIDA person identifier. |
| `INCM_YR` | Income year, stored as integer financial-year end year in current output. `2015` means FY 2014-15. | Present for every generated row. | DIL `INCM_YR`. |
| `OCPTN_GRP_CD` | Occupation group code. Current output is the first four digits of the synthetic ATO salary/wage occupation code. | `"0000"` means unknown or unavailable in the compact generator. | DIL occupation group code; tax-return occupation concept. |
| `SUB_OCPTN_GRP_CD` | Sub-occupation group code. Current output is a six-digit zero-padded ATO salary/wage occupation code. Most values are ANZSCO-style six-digit occupations or major-group `nfd` codes, and a small share are ATO special `9xxxxx` codes. | `"000000"` means unknown or unavailable. ATO `999000` means occupation not listed. | DIL sub-occupation group code. |
| `MN_BUS_TAX_OFC_ANZSIC_CD` | Main business or professional activity industry code. Current output uses a two-digit synthetic industry code from the spine. | `"00"` means unknown or unavailable. It is not a full workplace industry history. | DIL main business tax office ANZSIC code. |
| `CLNT_RSDNT_IND` | Client resident indicator. Current output sets this to `"Y"`. | Current generated values: `"Y"` only. If future output includes non-residents, document the valid code list and tax treatment. | DIL client resident indicator. |

Occupation and industry in tax data should be treated as broad context, not as
a definitive time-varying job history. In the current package, PIT_ITR can use
the occupation panel written by `generate_pit_ps()` where available, otherwise
it falls back to the spine occupation. The PIT_PS occupation panel deliberately
adds ATO-side reporting noise: most records retain the employment-panel
occupation, while calibrated shares are reported as the matching major-group
`nfd` occupation or as another occupation within the same ANZSCO major group.
The `nfd` rate is higher for Managers than other major groups. The panel also
uses the ATO salary and wage occupation code list's `9xxxxx` special codes:
apprentice/trainee codes are more common at younger ages, consultant codes are
more common among Managers and Professionals, and `999000` is a rare
occupation-not-listed fallback. This makes tax-return occupations less reliable
than Census occupation and targets about 80% exact 6-digit agreement between
ATO and Census occupation among comparable 2021 records.

### Income and loss variables

| Variable | Meaning and values | Missing, zeros, and subpopulation | Source concept |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GRS_PMT_TOTL_CALCD_AMT` | Salary or wages reported/calculated on the tax return. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated salary/wage amount on an observed return. Missing would be a schema issue. | DIL salary or wages; ABS uses this ITR item for employee income. |
| `BUS_INCM_TOTL_AMT` | Total business income. Numeric dollars in current output. | Zero means no generated business income. The current compact generator does not model the full set of business loss and primary/non-primary-production items. | DIL total business income. |
| `INTST_AMT` | Interest income amount. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated interest income. It does not rule out other investment income fields that exist in the full DIL but are not generated here. | DIL interest amount; ATO tax-return interest income concept. |
| `TI_OR_LSS_AMT` | Taxable income or loss after generated income and deduction components. Numeric dollars. | Can be negative. Current generator floors taxable losses at `-50000`. Absence from ITR means no lodged return, not zero taxable income. | DIL taxable income or loss. |

The current generator uses `PIT_PS` aggregate gross payments as the base for
salary and wages and then applies a small discrepancy model. This reflects the
fact that ITR salary and wages usually correspond closely to payment-summary
income but can differ because of corrections, amendments, timing, rounding, or
other reporting differences.

### Deduction variables

| Variable | Meaning and values | Missing, zeros, and subpopulation | Source concept |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DECLD_TOTL_WRK_DEDN_AMT` | Declared total work-related deductions. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated work-related deduction. Treat as the headline generated work-deduction amount. | DIL declared total work-related deduction amount. |
| `WRK_RLTD_CAR_EXPNSS_AMT` | Work-related car expenses. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated car expense. In real returns, deductibility depends on ATO rules and evidence. | DIL work-related car expenses. |
| `WRK_RLTD_CLTHG_EXPNSS_AMT` | Work-related clothing expenses. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated clothing expense. | DIL work-related clothing expenses. |
| `WRK_RLTD_TRVL_EXPNSS_AMT` | Work-related travel expenses. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated travel expense. | DIL work-related travel expenses. |
| `WRK_RLTD_OTHR_EXPNSS_AMT` | Other work-related expenses. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated other work expense. | DIL other work-related expenses. |
| `GIFTS_OR_DNTNS_AMT` | Deductible gifts or donations. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated gifts/donations deduction. | DIL gifts or donations. |
| `OTHR_DDCTNS_TOTL_AMT` | Other deductions total. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated other deductions. | DIL other deductions total. |

ATO deduction guidance emphasises that work-related deductions require an
expense incurred in doing the work, a direct connection to earning income, no
reimbursement, and records. The current generator creates plausible deduction
amounts but does not model substantiation, private-use apportionment, or every
deduction category in the tax return.

For downstream work, prefer `DECLD_TOTL_WRK_DEDN_AMT` as the headline
work-related deduction. Subcomponents are useful for testing category-specific
logic but should not be over-interpreted as a full ATO deduction schedule.

### Tax, offset, and balance variables

| Variable | Meaning and values | Missing, zeros, and subpopulation | Source concept |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GRS_TAX_AMT` | Gross tax calculated from generated taxable income before generated offsets and Medicare levy. Numeric dollars. | Zero can occur at low taxable incomes or losses. | DIL gross tax. |
| `LOW_INCM_ERNR_TAX_OFST_AMT` | Low income tax offset amount in current synthetic tax calculation. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated low-income offset. The current schedule is simplified and not year-specific. | DIL low income tax offset. |
| `BSC_ML_CALCD_AMT` | Basic Medicare levy calculated in the current synthetic tax calculation. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated levy because taxable income is below the simplified threshold. ATO Medicare rules vary by year and family circumstances. | DIL Medicare levy. |
| `NET_TAX_AMT` | Net tax after generated low-income offset and Medicare levy. Numeric dollars. | Zero means generated tax after offsets and levy is zero. | DIL net tax. |
| `BAL_PYBLE_RFNDBL_AMT` | Balance payable or refundable. Positive values mean payable; negative values mean refundable. | Missing would be a schema issue. It is calculated as generated net tax less aggregated PS tax withheld. | DIL balance payable or refundable amount. |

The current tax calculation is deliberately simplified. It uses a progressive
tax schedule, a low-income tax offset, and a basic Medicare levy. It does not
model every tax offset, HELP/SSL/AASL repayment, Medicare levy surcharge,
private health insurance rebate, spouse/family income-test interaction,
franking credits, refundable offsets, or all year-specific tax schedules.

### Joining ITR sub-tables

The four compact ITR sub-tables for a year should have the same row keys.
A typical analysis join is:

```r
itr <- context |>
  left_join(inc_loss, by = c("SYNTHETIC_AEUID", "INCM_YR")) |>
  left_join(ded_exp_off, by = c("SYNTHETIC_AEUID", "INCM_YR")) |>
  left_join(whld_debt, by = c("SYNTHETIC_AEUID", "INCM_YR"))
```

After joining, derived concepts should be labelled as tax-return concepts, for
example `tax_return_salary_wages`, `taxable_income_or_loss`, or
`balance_payable_refundable`. Avoid labels such as `employment_income_universe`
unless non-lodgers have been handled explicitly.

## PIT_IE: ABS Derived Income

### Row unit

`PIT_IE` is a person-financial-year derived income table. ABS describes admin
income calculations as using several PLIDA sources, including PS and ITR, to
estimate income types. The current package implements a compact derived-income
table with total income, broad income components, component earner flags, and a
source flag for wages and salary.

The current generator includes people aged 15 to 80 in the financial year and
skips rows with effectively zero generated income.

### Current fplida variables

| Variable | Meaning and values | Missing, zeros, and subpopulation | Source concept |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SYNTHETIC_AEUID` | Synthetic ATO person identifier. | Present for every generated derived-income row. | PLIDA person identifier. |
| `FIN_YEAR` | Financial-year string such as `"2019-20"`. | Present for every generated row. Normalise before joining to integer `PIT_PS` or `PIT_ITR` years. | DIL reference financial year. |
| `INCOME_EDITED` | Edited derived income amount. Numeric dollars. Current output is generated total income plus editing noise. | Can differ from `TOTALINC`. A small negative value is possible if editing noise exceeds a small positive total. | ABS derived income edited concept. |
| `WANDS` | Wages and salary, or employee income amount. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated employee income component. | DIL employee income amount. |
| `WANDS_EARNER` | Employee-income earner flag. Current generated values are `"E"` and `"N"`. | `"E"` means `WANDS` is non-zero; `"N"` means no generated employee income component. | DIL employee income earner flag. |
| `INVINC` | Investment income amount. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated investment income. | DIL investment income amount. |
| `INVINC_EARNER` | Investment-income earner flag. Current generated values are `"E"` and `"N"`. | `"E"` means `INVINC` is non-zero; `"N"` means no generated investment income. | DIL investment income earner flag. |
| `OWNUNINC` | Own unincorporated business income amount. Numeric dollars. | Can be negative in current output. Zero means no generated own-business income. | DIL own unincorporated business income concept. |
| `OWNUNINC_EARNER` | Own-business income earner flag. Current generated values are `"E"` and `"N"`. | `"E"` means `OWNUNINC` is non-zero; `"N"` means no generated own-business income. | DIL own-business income earner flag. |
| `SUPINC` | Superannuation and annuity income amount. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated superannuation or annuity income. Current generator makes this more common from age 60. | DIL superannuation and annuity income amount. |
| `SUPINC_EARNER` | Superannuation-income earner flag. Current generated values are `"E"` and `"N"`. | `"E"` means `SUPINC` is non-zero; `"N"` means no generated superannuation or annuity income. | DIL superannuation income earner flag. |
| `OTHINC` | Other income amount. Numeric dollars. | Zero means no generated other income. | DIL other income amount. |
| `OTHINC_EARNER` | Other-income earner flag. Current generated values are `"E"` and `"N"`. | `"E"` means `OTHINC` is non-zero; `"N"` means no generated other income. | DIL other income earner flag. |
| `TOTALINC` | Sum of generated component income amounts before editing noise. Numeric dollars. | Can differ from `INCOME_EDITED`. Use this when testing arithmetic component consistency. | DIL total income amount. |
| `TOTALINC_EARNER` | Total-income earner flag. Current generated values are `"E"` and `"N"`. | `"E"` means `TOTALINC` is non-zero; `"N"` means no generated total income. | DIL total income earner flag. |
| `NONLODGER` | Source of wages and salary amount. Current generated values are `"ITR"` and `"PS"`. | `"PS"` means a PS-only wages source in the current generator; `"ITR"` means tax-return source. It is not a general missingness flag. | DIL source of wages and salary amount. |

The local DIL also contains `NONLODGER_EARNER` in some PIT_IE tables, but the
current compact generator does not emit it. If added later, document its valid
code list separately rather than overloading `NONLODGER`.

### Derived-income components

For current output, the broad component relationship is:

```r
pit_ie_checked <- pit_ie |>
  mutate(
    component_total =
      coalesce(WANDS, 0) +
      coalesce(INVINC, 0) +
      coalesce(OWNUNINC, 0) +
      coalesce(SUPINC, 0) +
      coalesce(OTHINC, 0),
    edited_difference = INCOME_EDITED - TOTALINC
  )
```

`TOTALINC` should be interpreted as the generated component total.
`INCOME_EDITED` should be interpreted as the package's edited income amount.
Use `INCOME_EDITED` when the analysis is meant to mimic ABS edited income; use
components and `TOTALINC` when testing income-source composition.

## Recommended downstream derivations

### Person-year PIT panel

A useful person-year panel can combine PS, ITR, and IE while keeping the source
distinctions visible:

```r
ps_person_year <- pit_ps |>
  group_by(SYNTHETIC_AEUID, FINANCIAL_YEAR) |>
  summarise(
    ps_employers = n_distinct(EMPLOYER_ABN),
    ps_gross_payments = sum(coalesce(GROSS_PAYMENTS, 0)),
    ps_allowances = sum(coalesce(ALLOWANCES, 0)),
    ps_tax_withheld = sum(coalesce(TAX_WITHHELD, 0)),
    ps_reportable_fbt = sum(coalesce(REPORTABLE_FBT, 0)),
    ps_synthetic_sg = sum(coalesce(SUPER_GUARANTEE, 0)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

itr_person_year <- itr_context |>
  left_join(itr_inc_loss, by = c("SYNTHETIC_AEUID", "INCM_YR")) |>
  left_join(itr_ded_exp_off, by = c("SYNTHETIC_AEUID", "INCM_YR")) |>
  left_join(itr_whld_debt, by = c("SYNTHETIC_AEUID", "INCM_YR")) |>
  rename(FINANCIAL_YEAR = INCM_YR)

pit_panel <- ps_person_year |>
  full_join(itr_person_year, by = c("SYNTHETIC_AEUID", "FINANCIAL_YEAR")) |>
  mutate(
    has_ps = !is.na(ps_gross_payments),
    has_itr = !is.na(TI_OR_LSS_AMT),
    ps_only = has_ps & !has_itr
  )
```

This keeps non-lodgement visible. Do not silently convert missing ITR rows to
zero taxable income.

### Income labels

Recommended labels:

| Label | Use? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `ps_gross_payments` | Yes | Directly tied to payment-summary gross payments. |
| `ps_employee_cash_income` | Yes, if component definition is stated. | Useful annual PS concept when gross, allowances, and relevant lump sums are explicit. |
| `tax_return_salary_wages` | Yes | Clear that the amount comes from ITR salary/wages. |
| `taxable_income_or_loss` | Yes | Matches the tax-return concept. |
| `derived_total_income` | Yes | Clear `PIT_IE` source. |
| `edited_income` | Yes | Clear `PIT_IE` edited amount. |
| `employment_income` | Maybe | Ambiguous unless the source and components are stated. |
| `earnings` | Maybe | Acceptable only with explicit PS, ITR, or derived-income source labels. |
| `tax paid` | No for `NET_TAX_AMT` alone | `NET_TAX_AMT` is calculated tax liability, while actual payments/refunds depend on withholding and balance. |

## Validation checks

The PIT tests and data checks should cover both table shape and semantic
relationships.

Required shape checks:

- `generate_pit_ps()` writes one parquet file per requested financial year.
- `generate_pit_itr()` fails clearly if matching `PIT_PS` files are absent.
- For each generated ITR year, the four sub-tables exist and have identical
  `SYNTHETIC_AEUID` and `INCM_YR` keys.
- `generate_pit_ie()` writes the requested year files and uses the documented
  financial-year filename convention.
- Generated columns match either the current compact schema documented here or,
  if the generator is made DIL-shaped later, the DIL variables in
  `inst/plida_metadata/variables.csv`.

Required amount-semantics checks:

- Person-year ITR salary/wages are highly correlated with aggregated PS gross
  payments but are not required to be exactly equal.
- ITR filers are a subset of person-years with generated PS records under the
  current generator.
- `BAL_PYBLE_RFNDBL_AMT` equals `NET_TAX_AMT` less aggregated generated PS tax
  withheld.
- `NET_TAX_AMT` reflects the current simplified gross-tax, low-income-offset,
  and Medicare-levy calculation.
- `PIT_IE` `TOTALINC` equals the sum of income components before editing noise.
- `PIT_IE` component earner flags are `"E"` exactly when the corresponding
  component is non-zero, otherwise `"N"`.
- `PIT_IE` `NONLODGER` uses only `"ITR"` and `"PS"` in current output.

Known semantic caveats to keep visible:

- `SUPER_GUARANTEE` in compact `PIT_PS` is a local synthetic SG-style amount,
  not the same as official reportable employer superannuation contributions.
- `UNION_FEES` in compact `PIT_PS` is an implementation field backed only by an
  external ATO deduction concept; no same-dataset PIT_PS metadata support was
  found.
- `WORKPLACE_GIVING` in compact `PIT_PS` is an implementation field backed by
  external ATO/STP concepts; no same-dataset PIT_PS metadata support was found.
- `PIT_PS` lacks period dates, so it cannot exactly reproduce ABS current-income
  divisor methods.
- `PIT_ITR` does not represent non-lodgers.
- `PIT_ITR` tax calculations are simplified and not year-complete.
- `PIT_IE` is derived income and should not be used as raw tax assessment data.

## Promotion path

If this note becomes user-facing, the least disruptive path is:

1. Move or copy this file to `vignettes/pit-dataset-explainer.qmd`.
2. Add any package-level vignette dependencies to `DESCRIPTION`.
3. Decide whether to include executable validation chunks or keep the document
   as a static explainer.
4. Resolve the compact-schema versus DIL-schema question for PIT. If PIT stays
   compact, keep the crosswalk tables. If PIT becomes DIL-shaped, rewrite the
   variable tables around raw DIL names.
5. Add the ALife manual as a local source if access permits, and use it to
   refine the ATO PIT variable crosswalks.
6. Add a rendered article route if the package later uses a website or
   `pkgdown`.
